definitions.name: dao_voting_threshold_PercentageThreshold
definitions.description:
A percentage of voting power that must vote yes for a proposal to
pass. An example of why this is needed:

If a user specifies a 60% passing threshold, and there are 10
voters they likely expect that proposal to pass when there are 6
yes votes. This implies that the condition for passing should be
`vote_weights >= total_votes * threshold`.

With this in mind, how should a user specify that they would like
proposals to pass if the majority of voters choose yes? Selecting
a 50% passing threshold with those rules doesn't properly cover
that case as 5 voters voting yes out of 10 would pass the
proposal. Selecting 50.0001% or or some variation of that also
does not work as a very small yes vote which technically makes the
majority yes may not reach that threshold.

To handle these cases we provide both a majority and percent
option for all percentages. If majority is selected passing will
be determined by `yes > total_votes * 0.5`. If percent is selected
passing is determined by `yes >= total_votes * percent`.

In both of these cases a proposal with only abstain votes must
fail. This requires a special case passing logic.

majority.description: The majority of voters must vote yes for the proposal to pass.

percent.description:
A percentage of voting power >= percent must vote yes for the
proposal to pass.

definitions.name: dao_voting_threshold_PercentageThreshold
definitions.description:
A percentage of voting power that must vote yes for a proposal to
pass. An example of why this is needed:

If a user specifies a 60% passing threshold, and there are 10
voters they likely expect that proposal to pass when there are 6
yes votes. This implies that the condition for passing should be
`vote_weights >= total_votes * threshold`.

With this in mind, how should a user specify that they would like
proposals to pass if the majority of voters choose yes? Selecting
a 50% passing threshold with those rules doesn't properly cover
that case as 5 voters voting yes out of 10 would pass the
proposal. Selecting 50.0001% or or some variation of that also
does not work as a very small yes vote which technically makes the
majority yes may not reach that threshold.

option for all percentages. If majority is selected passing will
be determined by `yes > total_votes * 0.5`. If percent is selected
passing is determined by `yes >= total_votes * percent`.

In both of these cases a proposal with only abstain votes must
fail. This requires a special case passing logic.

percent.description:

proposal to pass.

enabled and will not be checked.

delegate with delegations has voted, or all delegators have overridden

definitions.name: dao_voting_threshold_PercentageThreshold
definitions.description:
A percentage of voting power that must vote yes for a proposal to
pass. An example of why this is needed:

If a user specifies a 60% passing threshold, and there are 10
voters they likely expect that proposal to pass when there are 6
yes votes. This implies that the condition for passing should be
`vote_weights >= total_votes * threshold`.

With this in mind, how should a user specify that they would like
proposals to pass if the majority of voters choose yes? Selecting
a 50% passing threshold with those rules doesn't properly cover
that case as 5 voters voting yes out of 10 would pass the
proposal. Selecting 50.0001% or or some variation of that also
does not work as a very small yes vote which technically makes the
majority yes may not reach that threshold.

To handle these cases we provide both a majority and percent
option for all percentages. If majority is selected passing will
be determined by `yes > total_votes * 0.5`. If percent is selected
passing is determined by `yes >= total_votes * percent`.

In both of these cases a proposal with only abstain votes must
fail. This requires a special case passing logic.

majority.description: The majority of voters must vote yes for the proposal to pass.

percent.description:
A percentage of voting power >= percent must vote yes for the
proposal to pass.

Whether or not the vetoer can execute a proposal early before the
timelock duration has expired

timelock_duration.description:
The time duration to lock a proposal for after its expiration to allow
the vetoer to veto.

definitions.name: cosmwasm_std_ibc_IbcMsg
definitions.description:
These are messages in the IBC lifecycle. Only usable by IBC-enabled contracts
(contracts that directly speak the IBC protocol via 6 entry points)

close_channel.description:
This will close an existing channel that is owned by this contract.
Port is auto-assigned to the contract's IBC port

send_packet.description:
Sends an IBC packet with given data over the existing channel.
Data should be encoded in a format defined by the channel version,
and the module on the other side should know how to parse this.

timeout.description: when packet times out, measured on remote chain

transfer.description:
Sends bank tokens owned by the contract to the given address on another chain.
The channel must already be established between the ibctransfer module on this chain
and a matching module on the remote chain.
We cannot select the port_id, this is whatever the local chain has bound the ibctransfer
module to.

amount.description:
packet data only supports one coin
https://github.com/cosmos/cosmos-sdk/blob/v0.40.0/proto/ibc/applications/transfer/v1/transfer.proto#L11-L20

channel_id.description: existing channel to send the tokens over

memo.description:
An optional memo. See the blog post
["Moving Beyond Simple Token Transfers"](https://medium.com/the-interchain-foundation/moving-beyond-simple-token-transfers-d42b2b1dc29b)
for more information.

There is no difference between setting this to `None` or an empty string.

This field is only supported on chains with CosmWasm >= 2.0 and silently
ignored on older chains.
If you need support for both 1.x and 2.x chain with the same codebase,
it is recommended to use `CosmosMsg::Stargate` with a custom MsgTransfer
protobuf encoder instead.

timeout.description: when packet times out, measured on remote chain

to_address.description: address on the remote chain to receive these tokens

write_acknowledgement.description:
Acknowledges a packet that this contract received over IBC.
This allows acknowledging a packet that was not acknowledged yet in the `ibc_packet_receive` call.

channel_id.description: Existing channel where the packet was received

packet_sequence.description: Sequence number of the packet that was received

definitions.name: dao_voting_threshold_PercentageThreshold
definitions.description:
A percentage of voting power that must vote yes for a proposal to
pass. An example of why this is needed:

If a user specifies a 60% passing threshold, and there are 10
voters they likely expect that proposal to pass when there are 6
yes votes. This implies that the condition for passing should be
`vote_weights >= total_votes * threshold`.

With this in mind, how should a user specify that they would like
proposals to pass if the majority of voters choose yes? Selecting
a 50% passing threshold with those rules doesn't properly cover
that case as 5 voters voting yes out of 10 would pass the
proposal. Selecting 50.0001% or or some variation of that also
does not work as a very small yes vote which technically makes the
majority yes may not reach that threshold.

To handle these cases we provide both a majority and percent
option for all percentages. If majority is selected passing will
be determined by `yes > total_votes * 0.5`. If percent is selected
passing is determined by `yes >= total_votes * percent`.

In both of these cases a proposal with only abstain votes must
fail. This requires a special case passing logic.

majority.description: The majority of voters must vote yes for the proposal to pass.

percent.description:
A percentage of voting power >= percent must vote yes for the
proposal to pass.

early_execute.description:
Whether or not the vetoer can execute a proposal early before the
timelock duration has expired

timelock_duration.description:
The time duration to lock a proposal for after its expiration to allow
the vetoer to veto.

veto_before_passed.description: Whether or not the vetoer can veto a proposal before it passes.

vetoer.description: The address able to veto proposals.
